name: California

law.statute: California Retail Food Code (CalCode) Cottage Food Operations
law.key_section: Cottage Food Operations (Class A registration / Class B permit)

gate.regulator_fallback: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) (approved food list and statewide standards)
gate.mechanism: Class A: registration with local environmental health for direct-to-consumer sales only (self-certification; no routine kitchen inspection). Class B: permit with local environmental health for direct and indirect (retail/restaurant) sales; initial inspection and typically annual inspection. Both classes limited to CDPH-approved cottage foods and inflation-adjusted gross sales caps. Operator must complete approved cottage food training within 3 months of registration or permit.
gate.fee_notes: Fees are set by the local environmental health agency. Class A primary sales_cap field stores $75,000 statutory base; Class B statutory base is $150,000. CDPH adjusts both annually for California CPI (confirm current-year adjusted figures on CDPH before publishing dollar claims beyond the base).
gate.timing: before operating; complete cottage food operator training within 3 months of registration or permit

prohibited_foods: Foods not on the CDPH approved cottage food list
Potentially hazardous foods outside cottage food scope

channels.render_reason: Class A direct only; Class B adds indirect retail. Mail/third-party delivery allowed for direct sales per CDPH/local guidance within California.
channels.notes: Class A: direct sales only (in person, mail, or third-party delivery within California). Class B: direct plus indirect sales through permitted retailers. Advertisements that offer cottage food to the public must include county of approval, permit/registration number, and Made in a Home Kitchen (or Repackaged in a Home Kitchen).

labelling.basis: California Retail Food Code cottage food labeling requirements
required_elements: Name and address of the cottage food operation
Ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight
Mandated Made in a Home Kitchen statement (minimum type size per CalCode/local guidance)
labelling.allergen_rule: Major allergens declared per applicable labeling rules

training.free_training_name: Approved cottage food operator food processor course

premises.inspection_frequency_basis: Class A: no initial or routine kitchen inspection (self-certification). Class B: initial inspection and typically annual routine inspection by local EH.
premises.construction_standard: Private home kitchen and attached storage used for the cottage food operation; employee limit of one full-time equivalent excluding household members

unique.quirk_paragraph:
California splits cottage food into Class A and Class B. Class A is registration for direct sales. Class B is a permit that unlocks indirect sales to retailers, with kitchen inspection.

sales_cap in this record stores the Class A statutory base of $75,000 gross. Class B's statutory base is $150,000. CDPH adjusts both annually using California CPI, so live dollar caps move each year.

A second, separate regime is the Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operation (MEHKO). MEHKO is a county opt-in program for preparing and serving meals from a home kitchen. It is not the same as cottage food, and counties that have opted in are not listed here.
unique.common_mistake: Selling through stores on a Class A registration, or treating MEHKO meal service rules as cottage food rules.
unique.what_does_not_apply: Foods off the CDPH approved list, and MEHKO meal service (separate county opt-in program).

information_gain: Class A registration vs Class B permit (business_class gate)
Class A $75,000 / Class B $150,000 statutory bases with annual CPI adjustment
CDPH approved food list is load-bearing
Training required within 3 months of registration or permit
MEHKO is a separate county opt-in home-meal regime
